description: ROVERSE is a Google Maps for Mars, an interactive map where anyone can explore the Martian surface, search landmarks and landing sites, and see rover routes, built using NASA's open Mars data. We're a team of high-school students passionate about space and coding.
summary:
ROVERSE is an interactive web application built to work like Google Maps for Mars. Every year, NASA collects massive amounts of Martian data, yet most of it stays locked in complex scientific archives that everyday people cannot easily navigate. ROVERSE solves this problem by turning raw satellite imagery and rover records into a clean, familiar map interface that anyone can explore right from their browser.
Users can switch between realistic orbital surface photos and color-coded elevation maps powered by NASA laser altimeter data to see the true depth of craters and height of mountains. The app also plots rover traverse paths across Jezero Crater, links waypoints to ground-level rover photos, and pins major scientific discoveries directly onto their exact coordinates. Combined with a terrain route planner and an AI Field Guide, ROVERSE makes Martian exploration accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts everywhere.
details:
What ROVERSE Does and How It Works

ROVERSE is an interactive website that works just like Google Maps for Mars. It takes real NASA satellite photos and space data and turns them into a simple, visual map that anyone can explore right from their computer or tablet. Users can zoom in and move around famous places on Mars like Jezero Crater. You can switch between normal surface photos and a color-coded height map to see how deep the craters are and how tall the mountains stand. The app also shows the exact path the Perseverance rover took, lets you click along the trail to see ground-level photos from the rover's view, and pins major NASA discoveries right where they happened. On top of that, you can plan routes between two spots, save your favorite locations, and chat with a built-in AI Mars Guide to ask questions about the planet.

Benefits and Intended Impact

* Easy Access to Space Data. NASA collects huge amounts of cool data from Mars every year, but most of it is hidden inside complicated science websites. ROVERSE puts this real data into a simple map that regular people can easily use.

* Helpful for Students and Teachers. The app makes learning about space fun and interactive for classrooms. Students can explore craters and rover paths hands-on instead of just reading long textbooks.

* Better Understanding of Mars. Seeing the hills, craters, and rocks around a discovery on a real map helps people picture what Mars actually looks like. It also shows how hard it is for rovers to drive safely across rough terrain.

* Inspires Future Explorers. Giving everyday space fans a tool to plan their own routes on Mars gets more people excited about future space missions.

Tools, Software, and Coding Languages Used

We built ROVERSE using the Base44 web app builder along with standard web coding languages like HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. To make sure our map and rover facts were real, we used public Mars maps and Perseverance mission records from NASA. We also connected an AI chatbot tool to power our Mars Field Guide in the side menu.

Creativity and Factors Considered

Our main creative idea was to make Mars feel like an interactive survival guide instead of just a boring, flat picture. By mixing top-down height maps, ground-level rover views, and a route planner into one dark-themed dashboard, users really feel like they are inside mission control. While building it, our team focused on making the buttons easy to understand, keeping the map fast to load, and explaining all the space facts in simple words so anyone can enjoy it.
